analysis:
All three changed files are test-only under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD. No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, or authorization paths change.

1. Fixtures/SSDCooperativePoolTestSupport.swift (new, lines 1-12) moves the existing `onGCD` helper out of SSDCacheEpochStoreTests.swift, where it was private. It now has internal visibility within the test target. It only wraps work in a DispatchQueue.global continuation, so there is no security surface.

2. SSDCacheEpochStoreTests.swift removes the private helper (base lines 8-15). Test bodies are unchanged and still use `onGCD` from the shared file. The epoch, rotation, symlink-rejection, bounded-record and wipe-race coverage for T-041 mitigations is retained and not weakened.

3. SSDWholeRootTelemetryConcurrencyTests.swift replaces PausedMaintenanceStore with SnapshotDuringSweepStore (head lines 11-58). It takes the heartbeat snapshot on a dedicated Thread inside the sweep's destructive-change barrier and bounds the wait to 5 s. This removes the risk of the test holding the shared budget lock indefinitely. Assertions still check that the snapshot is available during the sweep (head line 82), that the snapshot sees ttlExpired == 0, and that the final stats show ttlExpired == 1. The test still exercises the real removeItemIfSafe path under evictionRoot. Coverage of the TTL sweep and the telemetry-availability property (T-041, SEC-035 residual) is preserved. The change reduces test flakiness and does not alter production behavior.

No new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumptions were identified. Remaining integration question: none material. Production SSD cache code was not in the supplied scope and was not reviewed.
